module_title: Windows OS - Foundational Basics and Major Versions
introduction: Microsoft Windows is the most widely tested operating system in the 'Computer Knowledge' section of competitive exams (SSC, Banking, Railways). At this foundational level, we will focus on the fundamental visual interface of Windows (GUI), its evolution through iconic versions, and essential desktop elements.

core_concepts.title: What is Windows OS?
core_concepts.description: Developed by Microsoft, Windows is a Graphical User Interface (GUI) based operating system. It acts as a primary interface (middleman) translating human actions into machine-executable instructions for the computer hardware.

core_concepts.title: GUI (Graphical User Interface)
core_concepts.description: Before Windows, operating systems like MS-DOS required users to type text commands. Windows introduced the GUI, allowing users to interact with the system visually using a mouse to click on 'Icons', 'Menus', and 'Windows'.

core_concepts.title: Milestone Historical Versions
core_concepts.description:
- Windows 95: Introduced the revolutionary 'Start Button' and the 'Taskbar' for the first time.
- Windows XP: Released in 2001, it became one of the most successful, stable, and popular operating systems in history.
- Windows 7: Launched in 2009, highly praised for its speed and clean visual design.
- Windows 8: Released in 2012, it removed the traditional Start Button to favor touch-screens, which resulted in a massive commercial failure.
- Windows 10 & 11: The current modern standards for personal and professional computing.

important_entities.name: Desktop
important_entities.significance: The main workspace screen that appears immediately after the computer boots up and the user logs in.

important_entities.name: Taskbar
important_entities.significance: The horizontal bar typically located at the very bottom of the screen. It houses the Start Button, pinned application shortcuts, currently running programs, and the System Tray (clock, volume, Wi-Fi).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic trivia trap! Examiners frequently ask: 'Which version of Windows immediately succeeded Windows 8?' Many students guess Windows 9. In reality, Microsoft skipped the number 9 entirely and went straight from Windows 8 (and 8.1) to Windows 10 for branding and architectural reasons.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the acronym WIMP to recall the absolute basic visual elements that define a classic Windows GUI environment.

exam_strategy_tips: Tier-1 exams heavily favor basic navigational questions. Make sure you remember the primary purpose of the Taskbar, the location of the System Tray, and which version introduced the Start Menu (Windows 95).
